findings.title: TLS certificate expiring within 90 days
findings.description: The wildcard TLS certificate for *.techstride.io expires on 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z (72 days from scan date). Automated renewal should be verified to avoid service disruption.

findings.title: Admin dashboard routes discoverable via client bundle analysis
findings.description: Static analysis of the Next.js client bundle at store.techstride.io reveals internal routing for /dashboard/products, /dashboard/users, and /dashboard/orders. These paths are publicly enumerable. Client-side authentication redirects are the only control preventing unauthorized access â€” no server-side session validation is enforced on the Next.js page routes.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: Responses from store.techstride.io do not include a Content-Security-Policy header. Without a CSP, the browser permits inline script execution and resource loading from arbitrary origins, increasing the impact of any cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Server framework version disclosed in response headers
findings.description: HTTP responses from api.techstride.io include the X-Powered-By: Express header. Error responses additionally disclose the Node.js version. This information assists attackers in targeting known vulnerabilities.

evidence.error_response_leakage: Node.js v22.x.x stack trace visible in 500 responses

findings.title: Stripe webhook endpoint publicly accessible without IP allowlisting
findings.description: The POST /api/v1/webhook endpoint is publicly accessible from any IP address. Stripe recommends restricting webhook delivery to Stripe's published IP ranges. The endpoint does validate Stripe-Signature headers, but the absence of IP allowlisting increases the attack surface for signature bypass attempts.

findings.title: Product search endpoint accepts user-controlled query parameter without observable sanitization
findings.description: The GET /api/v1/products/search endpoint accepts a 'q' query parameter and reflects it in the context of the database query. Crawl-based analysis confirms the parameter is included in response metadata. Detailed validation behavior requires authenticated analysis.

findings.title: User list endpoint accessible without authentication — returns hashed passwords
findings.description: The GET /api/v1/users endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication. Response body includes email, role, createdAt, and hashed password fields for all registered users. Enumerated via active crawl.

findings.title: Application log endpoint publicly reachable â€” GET /api/v1/logs returns log content without authentication
findings.description: Active probe confirmed GET /api/v1/logs is accessible from external IP addresses without authentication. The response body contains timestamped application log events. No session token or authorization header was required.

findings.title: Password reset token transmitted as URL query parameter
findings.description: The password reset flow delivers the reset token as a URL query parameter in the reset link (e.g., /reset-password?token=<value>). Tokens in URLs appear in browser history, server access logs, and HTTP Referer headers sent to third-party resources. Any logging system capturing request URLs stores active password reset credentials.

evidence.token_in_server_logs: confirmed â€” access logs captured full URL including token parameter
evidence.referer_exposure: token present in Referer header if user navigates away before completing reset

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) â€” Confirmed Outbound Request to Internal Metadata Service
findings.description: Active probe confirmed that POST /api/v1/webhook/ping initiates outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled URLs. Probe request targeting the AWS Instance Metadata Service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) received a 200 response from the server, indicating the container made a successful outbound connection to the internal endpoint. Server response body contained the IMDS directory listing proxied through the application response.

out_of_band.notes: Response body contains IMDS directory listing proxied through application response. Sub-15ms response consistent with same-VPC routing. IAM credential path: /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/

findings.title: Redis port 6379 accessible from public internet
findings.description: Port scan of the ALB IP (54.236.112.83) and associated infrastructure detected TCP port 6379 accepting connections from external IP addresses. This is consistent with the security group configuration observed in prior assessments. No AUTH challenge was observed on connection.

evidence.banner: -ERR wrong number of arguments for 'PING' command

findings.title: New API endpoint discovered: webhook connectivity check
findings.description: A new endpoint POST /api/v1/webhook/ping was discovered during this scan period. The endpoint accepts a JSON body containing a 'url' field and performs an outbound HTTP request to the specified address. No authentication is required.
